summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests CBP-1019 combined with FOLFOX, with or without bevacizumab, pembrolizumab, or enzalutamide, in adults with metastatic solid tumors of epithelial origin that overexpress TRPV6. Study drugs are given on an outpatient basis: CBP-1019, oxaliplatin, leucovorin, 5-fluorouracil, bevacizumab, and pembrolizumab are given into a vein (IV), and enzalutamide is taken by mouth, with duration and frequency not stated. The record says the study evaluates safety and efficacy, but no specific primary outcome measure is listed.
summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa CBP-1019 combinado con FOLFOX, con o sin bevacizumab, pembrolizumab o enzalutamida, en adultos con tumores sólidos metastásicos de origen epitelial que sobreexpresan TRPV6. Los medicamentos del estudio se administran de forma ambulatoria: CBP-1019, oxaliplatino, leucovorina, 5-fluorouracilo, bevacizumab y pembrolizumab se administran por vena (IV), y la enzalutamida se toma por vía oral; la duración y la frecuencia no se indican. El registro indica que el estudio evalúa la seguridad y la eficacia, pero no se enumera una medida de resultado principal específica.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with metastatic or unresectable epithelial-origin cancer, other than ovarian cancer.
Prior standard therapy received, with disease progression or intolerable toxicity afterward.
Measurable disease of at least 1 cm, except prostate cancer patients who meet specified progression criteria.
Expansion cohorts include metastatic pancreatic or colorectal cancer with an oxaliplatin and irinotecan-free interval of at least 4 months, prior anti-PD-(L)1 t
ECOG performance status of 1 or less, adequate blood counts and organ function, and willingness to provide baseline tumor tissue.
not_for: Active infection requiring IV antibiotics, or symptomatic heart failure (NYHA Class III or IV).
Heart attack, unstable angina, stroke, or transient ischemic attack within 6 months before enrollment.
Congenital long QT syndrome, prior torsade de pointes, or family history of unexplained sudden death.
Known allergy to the study drugs or their components.
Major surgery within 28 days or minor surgery within 7 days before study entry, or a live vaccine within 30 days before the first dose.
